reset.subject: Reset your Release Radar password

reset.expiry: The link works once and stays valid for {minutes} minutes.
reset.ignore: If this wasn't you, you can ignore this message. Your password stays as it is.

welcome.subject: Your Release Radar account is ready
welcome.intro: An account has been created for you on Release Radar. Sign in with the details below.
welcome.change_notice: You'll be asked to choose your own password when you first sign in.

profile.name: News performance
profile.purpose: How far a release travelled: news pickups, Altmetric, EurekAlert and the university's website, each compared with releases of the same and the two previous academic years.

readme.title: Release Radar export
readme.scope_view: Rows: the releases shown on the Data page, {count} in all.
readme.state_value: A number was recorded. 0 is a real zero.
readme.state_na: N/A: the number can't exist for this release, such as Altmetric without a DOI.
readme.state_empty: Empty: not recorded yet, or not due yet.
readme.state_inferred: Inferred: where a column ending in “inferred” holds 1, the 0 before it was not entered. The paper was published on or after the release date, so it could have no Altmetric score before the release.
readme.flags: Yes-or-no columns, such as Embargoed: 1 means yes, 0 means no.
readme.year: Academic year: the year it begins in, so {year} runs from {first} to {last}. It comes from the release date.
readme.code_year: A release code keeps the year it was given, even if the date moved later.
readme.colleagues: A column with a name in brackets is that person's own field.
readme.personal: This file contains personal data, such as researchers' names. Keep it within the office and delete copies you no longer need.

readme.title: Release Radar: releases per writer
readme.counting: Each number counts releases by their release date. Releases without a release date, and removed releases, are not counted.
readme.totals: The last column and the last row are totals.
readme.undated: Not counted yet: {count} release(s) without a release date.
readme.personal: This file contains colleagues' names. Keep it within the office.

report.writer_without_account: Writes releases but has no account with this email yet: the writer is not linked to a user. Invite them in Settings → Users and import again to link.
report.column_not_imported: A column Release Radar has no field for: not imported. To import it, choose a shared or private field for it under Other columns in the workbook, and check again.
report.researcher_resolved: Surname only: read as {name}, the one author of the paper with this family name. Marked unverified.
report.researcher_unresolved: Surname only, and the paper's authors don't settle it ({matches} with this family name): kept as written, marked incomplete.
report.gender_conflict: This researcher's gender is recorded differently on another release: {kept} was kept.
report.skipped_no_title: No title and no DOI: not imported.
report.release_restored: This release had been removed in the app: it is back.
report.writer_unknown: Not in the Staff sheet: left without a writer.
report.unit_unknown: Not in the Units sheet: left without a unit.
report.crossref_not_found: Crossref does not know this DOI: the paper's journal, date and authors stay empty.
report.crossref_unavailable: Crossref did not answer: the paper's details stay empty. Import again later to fill them.
report.gender_unreadable: Not M or F: gender not recorded.
report.researcher_from_sheet: Taken from the Two-name releases sheet: {name}.
report.researcher_first_listed: Several names: {name}, the first, is the corresponding researcher; the others went to Also featured.
report.embargo_unreadable: Neither a date nor a dash: left as it was.
report.code_year_differs: The release date falls in AY{year}: the code keeps its own year (D35).
report.ea_url_unusual: Not a EurekAlert news-release link: kept, and marked on the release.
report.website_off_domain: Not on {domain}: website views don't apply to this release.
report.no_release_date: No release date: imported without one, so its numbers are not due yet.
report.not_a_number: Not a number: left as missing.
report.not_a_whole_number: Not a whole number, which this field takes: left as it is.
report.value_where_na: A number where the rules say there can't be one: kept.
report.skipped_unit_writer: Written by a unit, not by the office: not imported.
report.code_duplicate: Row {first} has this code too: this release gets {new}.
report.release_made_in_app: A release made in the app already has this code: the workbook's values go into it.
report.number_shown_as_date: A date in a number column, probably the number {number} formatted as a date: left as missing. Type the number in if that's right.
report.feedback_column_by_content: Read as {what}, by its content: its heading says nothing.
report.feedback_skipped_staff_test: The office's own test response: not imported.
report.feedback_linked_by_url: Linked to the release with this EurekAlert link.
report.feedback_not_linked: No release has this ID: the response is kept without a release.
report.feedback_release_removed: The release was removed in the app: the response is linked to it anyway.
report.feedback_other_text: Written in “Other” ({question}): kept as text on the response.
report.feedback_none_with_others: “None” ticked together with other answers ({question}): kept as given.
report.feedback_scale_unknown: Not a point on the agreement scale: this statement is left unanswered.
report.feedback_corrected: All three statements were “Strongly disagree”: corrected to “Strongly agree” (inverted scale, response {id}). The response's history shows both.
report.feedback_correction_not_needed: Response {id} was to be corrected for an inverted scale, but its statements are not all “Strongly disagree”: left as given. Please check.
report.feedback_all_disagree: All three statements are “Strongly disagree” (response {id}). An inverted scale, as with four earlier responses? Not corrected: please check.
report.fill_mode: Only what is empty in Release Radar is filled: nothing already there changes. New codes are added in full.
report.fill_filled: Empty in Release Radar ({field}): filled with the workbook's value.
report.fill_kept: Release Radar has “{current}” ({field}): kept, as only empty cells are filled.
report.fill_removed_left: Removed in the app: left as it is, as only empty cells are filled.

counts.researchers_linked: Researchers found already in Release Radar
counts.dashes: Numbers marked not applicable by a dash
counts.website_off_domain: Releases whose website views don't apply
counts.feedback_already: Responses already imported, left as they are
counts.feedback_linked: New responses linked to their release
counts.cells_filled: Cells filled because they were empty in Release Radar
counts.cells_kept: Cells where the workbook differs, left as they are

md.feedback_title_dry_run: Researcher feedback import: dry run (nothing changed)

states.insufficient: Too little data for a score

readme.title: Release Radar analysis: {name}
readme.title_top: Release Radar analysis: top and bottom 5 by {name}
readme.analysed: Analysed: {count} releases ({filters}). Medians, spreads, ranks and every score's comparison set come from these.
readme.shown: Shown: {count} of them ({filters}). The rows are these; they change no number.
readme.profile: Score profile: {name}, version {version}. Comparison set: the finished releases of the {years} academic years up to and including the release's own; a component needs at least {minimum} values there, and a score at least {coverage} % coverage.
readme.altmetric_increase: Altmetric: the increase from day 0 to day 28.
readme.rows: Rows: every shown release, highest first; those without a value come last.
readme.top: Rows: the five highest and the five lowest shown releases that are finished and have a value. No release is in both lists.
readme.rank: Rank: among the analysed releases with a value (for the score: finished releases only). Equal values share a rank. A provisional release shows the rank it would have.
readme.percentile: Percentile: the one the score uses, (number below + half the number equal) ÷ number compared × 100, within the release's comparison set. Empty when that set has too few values.
readme.score: Score: 0–100, the weighted mean of the component percentiles. Coverage: the share of the applicable weight with a value.
readme.provisional: Provisional (1): the release is less than 30 days old, so its numbers may still change.
readme.quartiles: Medians and quartiles on the Analysis pages are computed as Excel's QUARTILE.INC.
